prompt:
Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape 3:2, crisp vanilla Minecraft voxel style, plain light ivory background, sunlit, no characters or animals. Two views SIDE BY SIDE: LEFT straight-on orthographic front elevation of the ENTIRE row; RIGHT three-quarter view of the SAME entire row at the same scale. Fit every plot in both panels, no cropping. 96 blocks wide, 19 deep, one or two storeys, chimney tops about 20 blocks. Skilled human builder quality: substantial massing, recessed framed windows, projecting porches, stairs/slabs for roof verges/eaves/ridges, fences/walls/trapdoors/lanterns for fine detail. Small labels 0–7 identify plots; heading FRONT ELEVATION and THREE-QUARTER. Include a compact exact-block-id materials key if space allows.
A gravel mill-village lane with wheel ruts crosses the front, lantern posts every 12 blocks. Each plot has a picket fence and centered gate. WEST TO EAST in BOTH views:
0: Dogtrot house, two stripped_dark_oak_log pens under a single brown exposed_cut_copper side-gable roof, open central breezeway behind full-width spruce porch, cobblestone fieldstone chimney at back.

2: Tall white smooth_quartz I-house, one room deep, symmetrical THREE-bay facade, warped_trapdoor dark green shutters. Full-width TWO-storey porch, pale posts, railed upper gallery, quartz cornice, dark deepslate_tile_stairs/deepslate_tile_slab side-gable roof, slim bricks end chimneys on BOTH white gables.
3: Square four-room pale_oak_planks grey-white weatherboard cottage, red polished_granite_stairs/polished_granite_slab pyramid roof, ONE brick chimney at apex, full front porch.
4: Long TWO-storey mangrove_planks oxblood boarding house, stripped_pale_oak_log pale battens and belt course, SIX upper windows, long shed-roof front porch with spruce rocking chairs and hanging sign reading exactly BOARDING, olive-grey weathered_cut_copper roof, west chimney.
5: Fenced packed_mud/coarse_dirt work yard. Small stripped_dark_oak_log smokehouse, blackstone_stairs/blackstone_slab sooty roof and rear vent; hanging hams suggested with vanilla block props inside. Log woodpile beneath spruce_slab lean-to, water_cauldron wash kettle over sunken campfire, rinse barrels, spruce bench.
6: Three broad flat-crowned pecan analog trees using jungle_log and jungle_leaves/oak_leaves; picnic table and benches of spruce_stairs/spruce_slab, iron_chain swing from low limb, exactly FOUR beehives in cornflower and oxeye_daisy beds, one bee_nest beneath branch. No bees or other animals.
7: 1920s bricks bungalow with low oxidized_cut_copper front-gable roof sweeping over deep porch; tapered pale posts on brick pedestals, white trim, paired glass_pane windows, spruce_trapdoor louvred gable vent, exposed spruce rafter tails, bricks chimney on west slope.

changes: Generated with the built-in image tool and saved as concept.png in the current directory without post-processing.
The views are stacked vertically, rather than side by side. They are approximately the same scale.

This is raster concept art, not a block schematic: exact block identities, counts and dimensions cannot be verified. Added ids describe closest vanilla equivalents. The roles retain all planned blocks; some appear only in the materials key or are not visibly used.
The dogtrot roof is turquoise weathered or oxidized copper rather than brown exposed copper.
The 96-by-19 footprint, 20-block height limit and 12-block lantern spacing are not measurable from the image.
Most frontage fencing is brown rather than pale pickets; centered pale gates are inconsistent or obscured.
The camelback hump is stepped behind the front gable, but a complete two-storey rear volume is not clearly established.
The I-house has both brick chimneys, although the three-quarter view shows a substantial exposed brick strip on the end wall. Its one-room depth is not verifiable.
The boarding house has six upper windows. Its pale battens are faint, and the BOARDING lettering is imperfect, especially in the lower view.
The smokehouse interior and hanging hams are not visible. The rear smoke vent and sunken fire beneath the kettle are not clearly demonstrated.
The woodpile uses small rounded log-end forms and the chairs use thin furniture-like parts that do not consistently obey vanilla block geometry.
The orchard crowns are rounded and irregular rather than broad and flat. Overlap prevents confidently confirming three separate trees.
Four installed beehives and a wild nest under a branch are not clearly identifiable; beehive and bee_nest also appear as materials-key samples.
A chain swing and picnic furniture are suggested, but the picnic table and separate benches are not fully resolved.
The bungalow has pale porch posts, but their taper, brick pedestals and exposed rafter tails are weakly resolved.
Additional flowering borders, shrubs and grass extend along nearly every plot. Pink and purple flowers are interpreted as peony and allium.

Additional shape equivalents needed for visible details include stone_stairs, stone_brick_stairs, stone_brick_slab, pale_oak_stairs, pale_oak_slab and spruce_fence_gate. Centered gates and signage require pale_oak_fence_gate and spruce_sign beyond the original palette.
The materials key contains malformed labels, including misspellings of water_cauldron and beehive, and depicts some blocks with inaccurate textures or shapes.
